lines.trans: Before the movers cleared the house, I saved this box from the attic shelf.
Open the white paper... no way! Grandfather's carved wooden train!
Look underneath the wheels, your name and my name are still written in pencil.

words.gram: singular noun + 1st singular possessive, with و- (and)

lines.trans: I thought it was lost when we sold the house! Why did you keep it for me?
Because a house is stone and wood, Ziad, while family is what remains.
And you two boys kept the sweetest part of Number twelve right here.
Excuse me, madam... wait. That voice! Madam Suad, the piano teacher?!
Still waiting for you to play the musical scale slowly, Ziad!
Am I dreaming?! Did you plan this whole reunion, Rami?
Sweet luck, and one blue suitcase swapped on Monday morning's bus!
Life arranges sweeter melodies than we do, my dear boys.
Please sit with us, Madam Suad! Tell me I am not twenty-five years late for the lesson!

words.gloss: please go ahead / here you are!

words.gram: definite masculine singular noun, with عال- (on/at the)

lines.trans: See you!

meanings.note: Color adjective with feminine بيضا (beida) and plural بيض (biid).

examples.trans: We brought clean white sheets.
The gift is wrapped in white paper.

meanings.note: Elative of حلو (ḥilu), used for pretty, sweet, or nice.

examples.trans: It has the loveliest view of the courtyard.
This is the nicest day of the week.

meanings.note: The color blue.

examples.trans: The blue suitcase is in the luggage closet.
I have two blue teacups.

meanings.note: First person singular pronoun.

examples.trans: I am Nour, the new receptionist.
I am Salma from the kitchen.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنقذ, بينقذ).

examples.trans: Quick thinking saved breakfast!
You saved my whole trip.

meanings.note: Second person masculine singular pronoun.

examples.trans: Did you plant these herbs yourself?
Did you plan this entire meeting?

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun 'you' when addressing two or more people.

examples.trans: You are very kind people.
Hold the torch, both of you.

meanings.note: Command to a male to wait.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
The suitcase is still waiting for its owner.

meanings.note: Everyday noun for a person's or place's name; takes possessive endings directly (اسمي my name, اسمك your name).

examples.trans: What is your kind name?
My name is written here in the notebook.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'twelve'; before a singular counted noun it takes -r: اطنعشر دقة ('twelve chimes').

examples.trans: The clock tower chimed twelve!
Here is twelve dinars change.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of الاثنين ('Monday', and with ال also 'both / the two').

examples.trans: I started work on Monday morning.
Monday's bus arrived at seven.

meanings.note: The universal relative pronoun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: That is what I want.
The inn that keeps a stranger's bag safe.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: باصات.

examples.trans: The bus station is close to here.
The bus trip was comfortable.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببيع, بيبيع).

examples.trans: The hardware shop sells this size.
I thought it was lost when we sold the house!

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian word meaning both 'only / just' (بس نص كاسة 'just half a glass') and 'but' between clauses.

examples.text: بدي أقرأ الدفتر، بس مش ملاقي نظارتي!
examples.trans: I want to read the ledger, only I cannot find my glasses!
Just half a glass, please.

meanings.note: The musical instrument.

examples.trans: The sound of the piano is warm and calm.
I learned piano when I was young.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بيوت.

examples.trans: The old house has a lovely courtyard.
The neighbourhood houses are built of stone.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتأخر, بيتأخر).

examples.trans: Tell me I am not late for the lesson!
The bus was not even a minute late.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتبدل, بيتبدل).

examples.trans: A blue suitcase got swapped at the bus station.
The keys were never mixed up.

meanings.note: Indicates physical location beneath something.

examples.trans: Let us bring it downstairs into the light.
The wide desk is under the window.

تفضّل.gloss: to please come in / sit / go ahead / here you are

meanings.en: to please come in / sit / go ahead / here you are
meanings.note: Essential Jordanian hospitality verb used mostly in the imperative: تفضل (to a man), تفضلي (to a woman), تفضلوا (plural).

examples.trans: Please have a seat, ma'am!
Here you go, hot mint tea.

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian expression to express surprise or ask for confirmation, like 'really?' or 'seriously!'.

examples.trans: My grandfather's workshop was on this street.
Did you really finish all the work?

meanings.note: Standard word used in Jordanian Arabic for a part, portion, or section of something.

examples.trans: This is the sweetest part of the story.
I read the first part of the book.

meanings.note: Standard word for a stone or rock, singular form.

examples.trans: Old stone holds warmth.
She stepped onto the stone step outside.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أحلام.

examples.text: هاد كان حلم حياتي من زمان.
examples.trans: That was my lifelong dream.
At last our dreams came true.

meanings.note: One of the most frequently used adjectives in Jordanian Arabic to mean beautiful, sweet, nice, or good.

examples.trans: The strawberry jam is sweet and tasty.
The sweater looks lovely and warm.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun.

examples.trans: Life is sweet with kind people.
Never in my life have I seen a prettier view.

حِفِظ.gloss: to keep safe; hold onto; preserve

meanings.en: to keep safe; hold onto; preserve
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحفظ, بيحفظ).

examples.trans: Old stone holds the warmth until morning.

examples.text: شكرا لأنك حفظت الشنتة طول الأسبوع.
examples.trans: Thank you for keeping the bag safe all week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بخبي, بيخبي).

examples.trans: Why did you save it away for me all these years?
She tucked the recipe away in the kitchen notebook.

meanings.note: Used for the material wood or timber.

examples.trans: The wooden ceiling is warm and quiet.
This is a hand-carved wooden train.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بخطط, بيخطط).

examples.trans: Did you plan this entire meeting?
We planned to open the café in spring.

meanings.note: The number five, used in counting abstractly or before masculine counted nouns.

examples.trans: It is five to twelve.

examples.text: الدكان على بعد خمس دقايق مشي.
examples.trans: The shop is five minutes' walk away.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: دروس.

examples.trans: The piano lesson is every Friday.
I was not late for the lesson today.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برتب, بيرتب).

examples.trans: Life arranges sweeter melodies than we do.
I straighten my ties and keys every day.

meanings.note: Can mean the metal lead, or bullets. Often used in 'qalam rSaaS' (pencil).

examples.trans: We write bookings in pencil.
The name is written in pencil underneath.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: رفوف.

examples.trans: The gold tin is on the top shelf.
There are two pieces left on the shelf.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a number, digit, or phone number.

examples.trans: Here is your key, room number four.
Is there a phone number written on the paper?

meanings.note: Traditional Levantine domestic storage loft or overhead cupboard (السدة).

examples.text: خبيت هاد الصندوق من رف السدة.
examples.trans: I saved this box from the attic shelf.
The old suitcases are up in the loft.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: سلالم.

examples.trans: He played the musical scale slowly.
He climbed the ladder to fit the bulb.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a year.

examples.trans: The building is eighty years old.
I have not seen him for three years.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شوارع.

examples.trans: Our guesthouse is on a quiet street in central Amman.
There are old stone streets in the quarter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Universal Jordanian/Levantine word (from Turkish çanta) for any handbag, backpack, or travel suitcase.

examples.trans: This blue suitcase is very heavy.
We set the suitcases beside the reception desk.

meanings.note: Very common adverb in Jordanian Arabic for 'a little bit' or 'slowly'.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
Turn the valve slowly and gently.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken Jordanian noun for 'the morning' (الصبح in the morning, كل صبح every morning).

examples.trans: I drink black coffee every morning.
The morning bread is still hot.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: صدف.

examples.trans: What a sweet coincidence!
We met at the market by chance.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: صناديق.

examples.trans: The screwdriver is inside the toolbox.
We moved four boxes out of the hallway.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أصوات.

examples.trans: I heard the sound of rain on the window.
His voice is calm and polite on the phone.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بضيع, بيضيع).

examples.text: فكرت القطار ضاع لما بعنا البيت!
examples.trans: I thought the train got lost when we sold the house!
You will not get lost; the road is straight.

meanings.note: Very common Levantine verb meaning to stay, remain, or keep doing something.

examples.trans: Family is what remains.
My teacup stayed intact inside the suitcase!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: عمال.

examples.trans: The movers carried out the furniture in the morning.
Every worker in the bakery knows his job.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: عجلات.

examples.trans: Turn the blue valve wheel slowly.

examples.text: القطار الصغير إله أربع عجلات خشب.
examples.trans: The little train has four wooden wheels.

meanings.note: Extremely common colloquial conjunction used to indicate reason or purpose.

examples.trans: That is why the suitcase was heavy!
Are you polishing the lanterns for noon?

meanings.note: The number twenty.

examples.trans: We need twenty eggs for breakfast.
The ring's width is twenty millimetres.

meanings.note: Used both to get someone's attention politely ('excuse me') and to reply to شكرا ('you're welcome').

examples.trans: Excuse me, is the door locked?
Excuse me, Mr. Rami, sorry for the bother.

meanings.note: Can refer to a cardboard box, a tin can, or a small container.

examples.trans: The gold tin is on the top shelf.
I saved this old wooden box.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: علالي.

examples.trans: The attic room on the third floor is sunny.
We brought the boxes down from the attic.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: عيل.

examples.trans: The whole family gathers on Friday.
My family lived near here.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعزف, بيعزف).

examples.trans: I am still waiting for you to play the scale!

examples.text: الكبير كان يعزف بيانو كل جمعة.
examples.trans: The older boy used to play piano every Friday.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: غالية, plural: غاليين).

examples.trans: The wooden train is old and precious.
Welcome, my dear boys!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفتح, بيفتح).

examples.trans: The corner shop opens at seven.
Oh, the door finally opened!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفضي, بيفضي).

examples.text: أنقذت العلبة قبل ما العمال يفضوا البيت.
examples.trans: I saved the box before the movers cleared the house.
We cleared the boxes off the stairs.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفكر, بيفكر).

examples.trans: I thought it was lost when we sold the house!
We thought the matter through calmly.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقول, بيقول).

examples.trans: What does clause fourteen say?
He said thank you and hung up!

meanings.note: Preposition and adverb for time or sequence meaning 'prior to' or 'before'.

examples.text: علمت بيانو هون قبل خمسة وعشرين سنة.
examples.trans: I taught piano here twenty-five years ago.
Drink your coffee before the rush.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: قطارات.

examples.trans: The grandfather carved a small wooden train.
Children love playing with trains.

meanings.note: Past tense verb meaning to sit down, or sometimes to stay/remain in a place.

examples.trans: Please have a seat in the courtyard under the tree.

examples.text: ضيفة غرفة أربعة رح تقعد كل الأسبوع.
examples.trans: Room four's guest will stay the whole week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun; قلم رصاص means 'pencil'. Plural: أقلام.

examples.trans: I found my pen in the jacket pocket.
We write the names with a pencil.

meanings.note: A highly versatile quantifier used to mean 'all of', 'every', or 'the whole'.

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

meanings.note: Takes pronoun suffixes in spoken Jordanian: لأني (because I), لأنك (because you), لأنه (because he/it — also general 'because'), لأنكم (because you pl.).

examples.text: لأنه القهوة الطيبة بتخلي الناس لطاف!
examples.trans: Because good coffee makes people pleasant!
Thank you because you kept the bag safe.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: لحظات.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, let me read the line.
We waited a moment by the gate.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ألحان.

examples.trans: She played old melodies on the piano.
This gentle tune is familiar to me.

meanings.note: Very common Jordanian word to indicate that an action is ongoing or hasn't happened yet.

examples.trans: Is your cup still intact?
Nobody has written anything yet.

meanings.note: Core word in إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again / goodbye!') and also 'reunion / meeting'.

examples.trans: Goodbye, have a pleasant trip!

examples.text: كان لقاء دافي بعد غياب طويل.
examples.trans: It was a warm reunion after a long absence.

meanings.note: Common conjunction used to introduce a time clause, distinct from the question word 'when' (mita).

examples.trans: Smile when the bell rings!
When I get nervous, my sentences turn long.

meanings.note: The standard colloquial interrogative for 'why' in Jordanian Arabic.

examples.trans: Why did the person run off without his bag?
Why do you keep looking at the clock?

meanings.note: Used mostly as a negative particle for verbs ('didn't') or as a relative pronoun/conjunction ('what' or 'that which').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: محفورة, plural: محفورين).

examples.trans: My grandfather's hand-carved wooden train!
There are two initials engraved on the corner.

meanings.note: Polite everyday Jordanian address for an adult woman or female guest.

examples.trans: Good morning, madam, please come in!
The room is booked under Madam Suad.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: Standalone معقول! is a classic Jordanian exclamation of amazed disbelief ('No way! / Could it really be?!').

examples.text: معقول! قطار جدي الخشب لسا موجود!
examples.trans: Could it be! Grandfather's wooden train is still around!
The price is reasonable and fair for everyone.

meanings.note: In Jordanian speech, يا معلم is an affectionate, respectful way to address a boss or skilled craftsperson.

examples.trans: You are all generosity, boss!
She was a very gifted piano teacher.

meanings.note: Often used as a noun meaning 'letter' (mail) or 'destiny' in traditional contexts.

examples.trans: What is written in the letter, Nour?
Our two names are still written in pencil.

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: موسيقية, plural: موسيقيين).

examples.trans: Play the musical scale slowly.
She has a sensitive musical ear.

meanings.note: Everyday demonstrative pronoun for masculine singular objects.

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.note: Standard adverb for physical location.

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
Stay right here a minute.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun 'she' or 'it' (feminine).

examples.trans: Take a piece of bread while it is hot.
Family is what remains.

meanings.note: Collective noun used for paper material or leaves of a tree.

examples.trans: We use a paper ledger and a pencil.
He wrote a note on a small slip of paper.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ولاد.

examples.trans: The two boys learned piano together.
May you be blessed, my dear boys.

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ياسمين.

examples.trans: The jasmine vine climbs above the door.
The evening scent of jasmine lifts the spirit.

meanings.note: Standard noun for day, often used in expressions like 'el-yom' (today).

examples.trans: Today the weather is sunny and warm in Amman.
Have a happy, successful day!
